newsitem.title: UK: European Aviation buys BA surplus spares.
newsitem.headline: European Aviation buys BA surplus spares.

text.p: UK company European Aviation Ltd has purchased a major package of British Airways Plc surplus spares stock for "a substantial sum", said its managing director Trevor Whetter.
He added that Ledbury, Hertfordshire-based European Aviation would consider buying further commercial aircraft spares from BA if and when they became available.
But he stressed that the acquisition did not represent a step towards taking over part of all of BA's maintenance operation.
Whetter said his group was made up of an airline (European Aviation Air Charter), an aircraft spares company and a maintenance company.
"The BA spares acquisition will allow us to extend our aircraft support business on a more international basis," he told Reuters.
When contacted, BA gave no immediate response to the components' sale.
Whetter said the BA spares purchased were a mixture of components for McDonnell Douglas DC-10, Airbus A320 and Lockheed L10-11 TriStar aircraft and Boeing planes ranging from the 737 to 767.
"The new deal covers a great variety of parts, through flying surfaces and structural components to such items as galley equipment and cabin furnishings," said Whetter.

"There is a substantial number of aircraft flown by small carriers which do not have the space needed, or indeed the finance, to stock the myriad of components necessary to keep modern aircraft safely in the air. Our support is worldwide and 24 hours," he added.
